**Introduction to the "East Sea Optical Cable":**  
The East Sea Optical Cable is a critical communication infrastructure laid across the seabed of the East China Sea, facilitating high-speed data transmission between coastal regions and offshore areas. Designed to withstand underwater environmental challenges, it supports telecommunications, internet connectivity, and maritime surveillance. Its route and low cable winding density (as noted in maintenance reports) help minimize damage risks, ensuring reliable connectivity for commercial, military, and civilian use. The cable’s maintenance involves regular inspections and repairs to preserve its operational integrity, as outlined in undersea cable maintenance manuals.
